title: api: schema versioning, beta-header handling, and legacy response shims
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: we need a stable migration path for API consumers as we iterate on request/response schemas for streaming, function/tool calling, and structured output. This change adds a first-class API schema versioning mechanism, a temporary beta header for experimental schemas, and lightweight backward-compatibility shims to preserve behavior for older clients (including the OpenAI compatibility layer). Goals: 1) allow safe opt-in of new response shapes via X-Redwood-API-Version and X-Redwood-API-Beta headers, 2) surface deprecation notices in responses and logs when clients use legacy shapes, 3) provide sanity-preserving shims for the OpenAI compatibility layer to avoid breaking downstream SDKs and customer integrations, 4) ensure streaming stability across schema transitions, and 5) add integration tests and docs for the migration path. Summary of changes: Introduced api/versioning.py with a VersionRouter and a header-driven dispatch that validates requested schema versions and maps to internal contract adapters. Added openai_compat/response_shims.py to translate newer structured outputs into legacy OpenAI-style payloads when the compatibility mode is requested. Implemented deprecation-warning middleware that attaches a Deprecation header and records a structured telemetry event. Updated streaming codepath in api/streaming.py to enforce new framing rules for schema v2+ to prevent partial-function-call deliveries during reassembly. Added feature gate handling so that X-Redwood-API-Beta=1 enables experimental fields and returns X-Redwood-API-Beta-Expires to indicate sunset dates. Docs and tests: added docs/versioning.md and upgrade notes in redwood-docs/openapi.md. Added unit and integration tests in tests/test_schema_compat.py and perf canary cases that assert no regression in streaming latency. Rollout plan: feature behind a runtime flag. Stage 1: internal rollout to CI and staging, Stage 2: opt-in beta via header for customers, Stage 3: deprecate legacy behavior after 90 days with clear warnings and telemetry aggregation for compatibility issues. Checklist: - [x] Header-based version selection implemented - [x] Response shims for OpenAI compatibility added - [x] Deprecation warnings and telemetry events implemented - [x] Streaming framing fixes in place - [x] Tests and docs added - [x] Performance smoke tests run Known limitations: complex third-party tool calling schemas still require downstream SDK updates for full fidelity; shims intentionally drop experimental structured metadata rather than attempt lossy transformations. If customers need full fidelity we will provide explicit migration steps and a compatibility SDK update.

release_notes: Introduce API schema versioning. Add X-Redwood-API-Version and X-Redwood-API-Beta headers to opt-in to new request/response shapes. Provide temporary OpenAI compatibility shims to maintain existing SDK behavior. Streaming framing fixes for schema v2 improve stability during function/tool call reassembly. See docs/versioning.md for migration steps.
notes_for_support: If customers report missing fields when using older SDKs, ask them to set X-Redwood-API-Beta=0 or remove X-Redwood-API-Version header. For urgent incidents, toggle runtime flag to re-enable legacy behavior. Use telemetry event 'schema.compatibility.issue' to find impacted clients.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: clients may receive unexpected errors if they inadvertently opt into experimental schemas. Mitigation: beta header opt-in only, deprecation header and explicit 426 Upgrade Required responses, telemetry to track impacted clients and fast rollback via runtime flag.
upgrade_instructions: Clients can opt into the new schema by sending header 'X-Redwood-API-Version: 2' or 'X-Redwood-API-Beta: 1' to enable experimental fields. To remain on the legacy shape omit these headers. See redwood-docs/versioning.md for examples of SDK changes required to parse structured outputs and function/tool calling metadata.
